Penn directs hospital-record requests to the treating hospital, so routing needs to be confirmed for each record custodian, and outpatient office records may need to go directly to the physician's office. For personal injury attorneys managing multi-provider cases, that adds administrative work and delays that can stretch case timelines by months.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-powered medical record retrieval that handles Penn Medicine authorization requirements, provider follow-up, and error checking, typically delivering complete records in a couple of weeks.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


Penn directs hospital-record requests to the treating hospital, so confirm routing for each record custodian, including physician offices for outpatient records


-


The current Authorization for Disclosure form is UPHS-099-10, revised January 2026, and includes Yes/No selections for behavioral health and substance use disorder (SUD) records


-


For patient right-of-access requests, HIPAA generally requires action within 30 calendar days, with one possible 30-day extension after written notice


-

-


Pennsylvania's[2026 fee schedule](https://www.pa.gov/agencies/health/resources/medical-record-fees) caps copies at $2.00 per page for pages 1 to 20, $1.48 for pages 21 to 60, and $0.52 for pages 61 and beyond, plus a permitted search-and-retrieval fee of up to $29.61 for eligible requests

## **Understanding the Penn Medicine Medical Records Request Process**


### **Why Medical Records Are Essential for Legal Cases**


Medical records drive personal injury case valuation, damages, demands, and trial strategy, connecting the incident to the injuries and supporting future expense projections.


For attorneys handling Penn Medicine cases, the challenge is routing. A single motor vehicle accident case might involve emergency care at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania, follow-up orthopedic care at Penn Presbyterian Medical Center, and therapy at a Penn Medicine practice. Hospital records go to each treating hospital's records department, while office-visit records may need to go to the individual physician's office.


### **Key Steps in the Request Process**


The standard Penn Medicine records request workflow involves several steps:


-


Identify all treatment locations by reviewing intake notes, ambulance reports, and client interviews


-


Complete the authorization form with patient demographics, facility selection, recipient information, date ranges, and record types


-


Submit to each record custodian via fax or mail to the specific records department


-


Track and follow up with each facility independently


-


Process payment when invoiced (some facilities require prepayment)


-


Review for completeness after records arrive


For requests governed by HIPAA's[patient right of access](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/privacy/guidance/access/index.html) , providers generally must act within 30 calendar days after receipt, regardless of whether records are stored onsite or offsite. One extension of up to 30 additional calendar days is permitted if the required written notice explains the delay and provides a completion date. Attorney requests made solely under an authorization aren't automatically the same as patient-access requests. Turnaround varies with request scope, authorization issues, and record availability, so confirm receipt and expected completion with the responsible records department.


## **Official Penn Medicine Medical Records Request Form**


### **Downloading the Penn Medicine Authorization Form**


Penn Medicine uses a standardized[Authorization for Disclosure form](https://tupa-q-001.sitecorecontenthub.cloud/api/public/content/Authorization-for-Disclosure-of-Health-Information.pdf) (UPHS-099-10, revised January 2026) across its facilities. The form is also available in Spanish.


For multi-facility requests, confirm submission requirements with the relevant records departments.


### **Filling Out the Request Form Correctly**


The authorization form requires completion of several sections:


**Patient Identification:**


-


Full legal name (first, middle, last)


-


Date of birth


-


Current address


-


Phone number with area code


**Facility Selection:**


-


Check boxes for each Penn Medicine location with relevant records


-


Options include all Penn Medicine locations, individual hospitals, CPUP/CCA outpatient practices, and Penn Medicine at Home


**Recipient Information:**


-


Name of person or entity receiving records (law firm name)


-


Fax number


-


Complete mailing address


**Record Specifications:**


-


Start and end dates of care


-


Record types requested (discharge summary, operative report, lab reports, radiology, billing, etc.)


-


Delivery method: mail, CD, or email. Fax delivery is restricted to qualifying patient-care needs, even though fax can be used to submit the request


## **HIPAA-Compliant Release Forms for Penn Medicine Records**


### **Ensuring HIPAA Compliance**


Valid HIPAA authorization requires specific elements to protect patient rights while allowing legitimate disclosure. Penn Medicine's authorization form includes the core components required under 45 CFR 164.508:


-


Description of information to be disclosed


-


Identification of who may disclose the information


-


Identification of who may receive the information


-


Purpose of the disclosure


-


Expiration date or event


-


Patient signature and date


-


Right to revoke authorization


Penn's form sets authorization expiration at 180 days from the signature date. Check that the authorization remains valid when disclosure occurs, and obtain an updated authorization if necessary. Don't assume that approaching expiration or correcting a request automatically restarts an applicable legal deadline.


### **What to Include in Your HIPAA Release**


The sensitive records section deserves extra attention.[42 CFR Part 2](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/part-2/index.html) protects qualifying substance-use-disorder records and generally requires consent for disclosures unless an exception applies. Additional restrictions govern their use in proceedings against the patient. State laws also protect behavioral health information.


The current Penn Medicine form includes Yes/No selections for:


-


Behavioral health visits


-


Substance use disorder (SUD) visits


The form addresses other sensitive information through its accompanying acknowledgment, not a separate HIV/AIDS checkbox. Complete the applicable selections to clarify the authorized disclosure. Behavioral-health disclosure also requires hospital-representative validation, and verbal consent requires a second witness.

## **Accessing Your Medical Records Online: Penn Medicine Patient Portals**


### **Registering for Penn Medicine's Patient Portal**


Penn Medicine offers portal access through[MyPennMedicine](https://www.pennmedicine.org/patient-resources/policies/patient-access-health-information) , which provides free access to health records including test results, visit summaries, and medication lists. Lancaster General Health patients use a separate MyLGHealth portal, which has a separate login.


Patients and approved proxies can access records through the patient portal, subject to the applicable permissions. That doesn't mean an attorney automatically receives proxy access, so law firms still need written authorizations.


### **Limitations of Online Health Records**


Portals have real limits for legal use:


-


**Variable coverage:** Available dates and document types vary; check whether the portal contains the records needed for the case


-


**Incomplete record types:** Historical records, detailed billing, and departmental notes may be missing


-


**No third-party release:** Attorneys don't automatically get portal access to client records


-


**No legal certification:** Portal downloads don't include certification of completeness


For comprehensive legal documentation, written authorization requests remain the standard route.

## **Required Information for a Complete Penn Medicine Medical Record Request**


### **Essential Details for Authorization**


A complete authorization requires:


-


**Patient identification:** Full name matching medical records, date of birth, current contact information


-


**Specific date ranges:** Exact start and end dates rather than vague requests for "all records"


-


**Record type selection:** Check boxes for each category needed (discharge summary, operative report, labs, radiology reports, radiology images, billing, etc.)


-


**Recipient details:** Law firm name, address, and fax number


-


**Purpose of disclosure:** Select "Legal" or write "Legal representation"


-


**Signature:** Patient or authorized representative's signature, with the authorization still valid within its 180-day term


-


**Sensitive records authorization:** Complete the behavioral-health and SUD Yes/No selections


### **Avoiding Common Request Delays**


Cases may involve multiple record custodians. Review signatures, disclosure scope, and submission details before sending each request. Common preventable errors include:


-


**Incomplete signatures:** Missing patient signature, missing date, or signature by a representative without relationship documentation


-


**Wrong facility submission:** Sending HUP requests to Penn Presbyterian can delay processing


-


**Blank sensitive records section:** Leaving the behavioral health or SUD selections incomplete


-


**Vague date ranges:** Requests for "all records" or "everything" can slow processing compared to specific date ranges


-


**Lapsed authorization:** An authorization that's no longer valid when disclosure occurs


Incomplete authorizations are a leading preventable cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can delay or invalidate a request. Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.


## **Retrieving Medical Records for Legal Use Cases from Penn Medicine**

Princeton requests require separate New Jersey analysis


-

## **Ensuring Completeness and Accuracy of Penn Medicine Records Received**


### **Verifying Your Medical Record Set**


When records arrive, review them against your original request:


-


**Date range coverage:** Confirm records span the requested time period without gaps


-


**Record type completeness:** Verify all checked categories were included (billing, imaging, operative reports, etc.)


-


**Facility confirmation:** Ensure records came from the correct Penn Medicine location


-


**Patient identification:** Confirm records belong to your client and not another patient with a similar name


Under Pennsylvania's[hospital retention rule](https://www.pacodeandbulletin.gov/secure/pacode/data/028/chapter115/s115.23.html) , hospital records generally must be retained for at least seven years after discharge. For minors, hospital records must be retained until majority and then for seven years, or as long as adult records are maintained. Separate physician-record rules generally require seven years after the last medical service and, for minors, at least one year after majority if that requires longer retention. Princeton's New Jersey records follow New Jersey rules.


### **Addressing Discrepancies in Received Records**


If records appear incomplete:


-


**Identify specific gaps:** Note missing date ranges, record types, or facility records


-


**Contact the records department:** Call the specific facility to clarify what was included and what may have been missed


-


**Submit targeted follow-up:** Request specific missing records rather than repeating broad requests


-


**Document all communications:** Keep records of calls, faxes, and responses for the case file

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it take to get medical records from Penn Medicine?**


For requests governed by HIPAA's patient right of access, providers generally must act within 30 calendar days after receipt, regardless of whether records are stored onsite or offsite, with one possible extension of up to 30 more days after written notice. Turnaround varies with request scope, authorization issues, and record availability, so confirm receipt and expected completion with the responsible records department. Codes Health describes typical retrieval in a couple of weeks and uses request checking to help reduce preventable rejections. Penn Medicine-specific turnaround varies.


### **Is there a fee to request medical records from Penn Medicine?**


Usually, for third parties. Pennsylvania's 2026 schedule caps per-page copy charges (see above) and permits a search-and-retrieval fee of up to $29.61 for eligible requests. The schedule excludes search charges for patients requesting their own records and prohibits adding the search charge to certain flat-fee categories. Patient-initiated HIPAA access requests have lower fees limited to labor for copying, supplies, and postage. Penn Medicine Princeton Health requests require separate New Jersey analysis.


### **Can someone else request my medical records from Penn Medicine on my behalf?**


Yes, but specific authorization requirements apply. Attorneys and other third parties must submit a valid signed HIPAA authorization from the patient. For minors, the authorized signer depends on the treatment, who consented to it, the proposed disclosure, and applicable state law. Confirm the requirements for mental-health and other specially protected records rather than relying on a blanket age rule. For deceased patients, the estate executor signs with legal documentation. For incompetent patients, the legally authorized representative signs with guardianship papers, power of attorney, or court order documentation.


### **What if Penn Medicine cannot locate my medical records?**


First, verify you submitted to the correct Penn Medicine location, since hospital records are handled by the treating hospital and office records may sit with the physician's office. Check with the patient about exact treatment dates and locations, review ambulance reports for destination information, or contact Penn Medicine's central line at 800-789-7366 for help locating treatment records. For older records, review the applicable retention rule, keeping in mind that the end of a minimum retention period doesn't establish that records were actually destroyed.


### **Do I need separate authorizations for radiology images versus radiology reports?**


Not necessarily. Both can be selected on the same authorization; confirm any separate fulfillment instructions. The form includes separate checkboxes for "Radiology Reports" and "Radiology Images," so checking only one may get you the written interpretations without the imaging studies, or vice versa. For personal injury cases needing both, check both boxes. Note that radiology images delivered on CD aren't encrypted and may be accessible to others, as stated in the form's security notice.
